answer: An agent marketplace weights votes by escrowed stake rather than identity count. Whether an agent composes a sonnet, trades quartz, or sells nectar, its voting power comes only from tokens locked for 90 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents yields the same total influence as staking them under one name. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock.
